meta.title: Redact Secret — runtime credential redaction
meta.description: Redact Secret detects supported credentials while data is still in your application and replaces them before they reach logs, traces, tools, or AI context.

title: Secrets spread fast.
Stop them before they spread.
lede: A credential pasted into a prompt can end up in a tool response, a trace, a log, and a conversation history. Redact Secret detects supported credentials

lede.b: while the data is still in your application

lede: and replaces them before they reach those destinations.
hero.proof: One local detection core. Integrations for the paths your data takes.

io.caption: One scan
io.footnote: Synthetic fixture, not a live credential. The finding metadata records the family, offset, and length of the match, never the value.

problem.title: Protect live data, not just source code.
lede: Repository scanners help find secrets committed to code. Redact Secret works where your application handles text at runtime: user input, error messages, tool results, logs, traces, stored records, and model context.

lede.b: One paste becomes five copies before anyone notices.

problem.sourceNote: The application never asked for a credential. It arrived inside text the application does not control.

problem.remedy: Rotating the credential is the only remedy once it has landed. The scan belongs one step earlier, at the boundary where your application hands the text to something else.

integrations.title: Use the core directly, or connect it to the host you already use.
lede: One Rust detection core sits behind every package. Adapters wire it into logging, tracing, and AI workflows, so no host has to recreate the detection rules. The vault is a separate, opt-in way to restore what was redacted.

lede.b: Each card states what that package does not cover.

adapters.title: Adapters
adapters.lede: Host integrations. They make no decisions of their own: they pass text to the core and hand its answer back.

vault.title: Vault
vault.lede: Optional and separate. The core never keeps a value; the vault holds a mapping in memory only when you ask it to, and restores only under your policy.

core.title: Core library
core.description: Detection, policy, and redaction in Rust, with one API for JavaScript (Node.js and browsers), Python, and Rust.
core.coverage: Credentials by default. PII detection is opt-in and off unless you select it.

wasm.title: WebAssembly build
description: The browser build of the core. Installed automatically with
; not meant to be imported directly.
wasm.coverage: Runs on the page or in a Worker. The playground above uses it.

cli.title: CLI
cli.description: Reads standard input or one file and writes the sanitized text, for shells, pipelines, and hooks.
cli.coverage: Installed from crates.io, not npm. PII is opt-in with --pii.

web-stream.title: Web Streams
web-stream.description: A TransformStream that redacts text as it streams, shipped inside the core.
web-stream.coverage: There is no separate browser adapter package; this core subpath is the browser integration.

description: Redacts values in log calls and in the finished line, alongside
pino.coverage: Not object keys, and nothing a destination or transport adds after the line is written.

title: traces
otel.description: A dedicated trace adapter wraps the next SpanProcessor and redacts span names, attributes, events, links, and status messages.
otel.coverage: Attribute names are not redacted; spans the wrapped processor never receives are out of reach.

masking.title: Masking callbacks
description: createMaskSecrets() for hosts that hand you a value to mask, such as
masking.coverage: Covers only what the host routes through its callback.

ai-context.title: AI context
ai-context.description: Builds model context from user input and tool results. Fail-closed and all-or-nothing.
ai-context.coverage: Binary and encoded values are blocked, not decoded. Model output is not covered.

title: tool calls
mcp.description: Scans tools/call and resources/read results before they are logged, stored, or placed in context.
coverage: methods are out of scope; binary payloads block the result by default.

logging.title: Python logging
logging.description: A logging.Filter that adds value-based redaction to the standard library.
logging.coverage: Runs only where attached, so put it on every emitting handler rather than on the logger.

title: Python
otel-py.description: Wraps the next span processor in Python services.
otel-py.coverage: Installed only with the otel extra. A span that cannot be rewritten is dropped, not exported.

masking-py.title: Masking callbacks
description: mask_secrets for hosts that hand you a value to mask, such as
masking-py.coverage: Covers only what the host routes through its callback.

vault-browser.title: Vault
vault-browser.description: Replaces a secret with an opaque <rsv_…> token on the way to a model, and restores it only into a field you designate.
vault-browser.coverage: Main thread, or an opt-in dedicated-Worker mode qualified separately. No storage, no network.

vault-node.title: Vault
vault-node.description: The same in-memory capture and restore in Node.js 20, 22, and 24.
vault-node.coverage: Pins one exact core version; it does not install beside a different one.

vault-server.title: Vault server
vault-server.description: Authorizes every restore by principal, tenant, source, destination, and value path.
vault-server.coverage: In-memory is beta. The opt-in persistent profile is alpha and qualified only for its documented PostgreSQL profiles.

vault-py.title: Vault (Python)
vault-py.description: A native Python implementation of the vault server’s authorization contract.
vault-py.coverage: Research-grade on PyPI. Capture needs Node.js; persistent extras are published but not supported.

playground.lede: Edit the input and watch the output change. The detection core runs as WebAssembly in this tab, the same engine the packages ship.

privacy: It is not sent, stored, or logged, and spellcheck is off. Use synthetic values anyway: never paste a live credential into a web page.

boundary.title: Your data stays in your process.
boundary.lede: Detection and redaction run locally, without sending text to a scanning service. No network calls, no telemetry, and the same input always gives the same result.

pillars.title: Browser: preventive
pillars.body: A scan in the client catches a pasted credential before it leaves the device. Clients can be modified or skipped, so this scan helps but never enforces anything.

pillars.title: Server: authoritative
pillars.body: The server scans again, independently, before logging, storage, context construction, or model and tool invocation. That scan is the one your security decisions rely on.

title: Who enforces

body.b: Your application is what rejects the request.

body: Redact Secret does not stop anything on its own.

body: , not every secret or personal-data category.

body.b: An empty finding list is not proof that content is safe.

body: It never contacts a provider, so it cannot tell whether a detected credential is still active. It does not validate, rotate or revoke credentials, does not walk commit history, and does not replace a DLP platform.
